name: Annaly Capital Management, Inc.
moat_justification: Weak: scale ($135.6B assets, largest U.S. mortgage REIT), deep repo/swap market access and a diversified three-engine platform (Agency MBS, Residential Credit, MSR) are real but replicable advantages — the assets are commodity securities anyone with financing can buy, spreads are set by the market, and there is no pricing power. Measured returns confirm no durable franchise: fundamentals.json roic_proxy is null for every year (no operating-income tag is filed) and gross margin is null (no revenue tag), while ROE swung from -14.6% (2023) to +7.9% (2024) to +12.6% (2025) — rate/spread-driven, not franchise-driven.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 15.9%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md

CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED: the only cash tag filed for the latest fiscal year is the combined cash + restricted-cash total and no restricted-cash tag separates it — net debt is UNDERSTATED by the restricted amount (escrow / collateral / regulatory); check the balance sheet before trusting HIGH_NET_DEBT's absence
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low

TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.3%) vs bull-case tier C (10.5%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Diversified mortgage REIT with scale but no pricing power, moat 3/10 — on filing-direct TTM owner's earnings ($1.17/share) it cannot clear the 15% hurdle at $18.23 (weighted IRR 8.3%, weighted IV@15% $8.54; clears 15% only below ~$8.54); the 3-yr median base prints a fake Tier S off noncash mark-to-market addbacks and the company's own EAD ($2.92/share FY2025) reaches only Tier B — sector model misfit, confidence low.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: sector model misfit; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Scale and liquidity: largest U.S. mREIT, $9.4B of assets available for financing at YE2025, preferred access to repo and securitization markets
Diversified three-engine platform (Agency MBS / Residential Credit / MSR) — MSR and credit partly offset Agency spread risk across rate cycles
Internally managed (no external-manager fee drag) with a 25+ year operating history through multiple rate cycles
moat_against: No pricing power: Agency MBS spreads and repo funding costs are market-set; the product is a commodity financial asset
Structural leverage (GAAP 7.2x / economic 5.6x at YE2025) makes book value hostage to rate and spread moves
Persistent equity dilution: diluted share count +15.9%/yr CAGR in the engine history (ATM issuance), DPS cut in 2023 and 5-yr DPS CAGR -5.1% (fundamentals.json)
ROE is cyclical and sign-flipping (-14.6% in 2023) — no through-cycle return on capital above the cost of equity is demonstrated
